pr_title: fix: support dangling comma and throw on circular dependency in tsconfig
pr_body:
### Description

By implementing tsconfig resolve/parse/load logic in vite.
Much of the code is from the `tsconfig` package and thanks to @dominikg

Fixes #4481
Fixes #4512

### Additional context

`strip-bom` v4 is used instead of v5, because v5 is a native ES module, causing jest tests to fail.

No tests are added for the circular dependency issue because I don't yet know how to test it.

If we need better error messages, `json5` can be used.
I've considered using `jsonc-parser`, but it outputs error messages for trailing commas despite successfully parsing it.

---

😂 I've added the comma! It was formatted by prettier…
Should add `prettier-ignore` to the file

i've played with the idea of spinning tsconfig-parse as a new package - a more modern version of `tsconfig` package if you will. 

see also https://github.com/evanw/esbuild/issues/1515#issuecomment-897441858

let me know if you'd be fine with me reusing the resolution code and if you'd be willing to swap it out in vite then.

Yeah, that would be cool!

I worked on this PR mainly to unblock the release of v2.5.
A dedicated package would be better.

Regarding error reporting, JSON.parse error position should match the position in invalid tsconfig.json content so this should be enough here. Semantic errors would need either tsconfig schema validation or again using typescript api. I'll think about adding that to the package at some point then ;)

issue_context.title: [2.5 beta] circular references in tsconfig.extends result hanging devserver
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Using tsconfig.extends it is possible to create circular references. 

tsconfig.json
```js
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.circle.json"
  // ...
}
```
tsconfig.circle.json
```js
{
  "extends": "./tsconfig.json"
  // ...
}
```

The code that was addded in https://github.com/vitejs/vite/pull/4279 does not check this and runs forever, stalling the devserver.

note, the circular reference example is very short, it could be a lot less obvious

### Reproduction

```
npm init vite -t vanilla-ts ts-circle
npm i
# add circular reference tsconfig as shown above
npm run dev
# open devserver, it works bc tsconfig isn't read
npm run build
# fails, tsc correctly reports the circle
npm i -D vite@beta
# open devserver, it hangs, no errors on cli or browser console
```

### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: Linux 5.12 Ubuntu 20.04.2 LTS (Focal Fossa)
    CPU: (12) x64 AMD Ryzen 5 4600H with Radeon Graphics
    Memory: 6.86 GB / 15.07 GB
    Container: Yes
    Shell: 5.0.17 - /bin/bash
  Binaries:
    Node: 14.17.1 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v14.17.1/bin/node
    Yarn: 1.22.10 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v14.17.1/bin/yarn
    npm: 6.14.13 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v14.17.1/bin/npm
  Browsers:
    Chrome: 92.0.4515.107
    Firefox: 90.0.2
  npmPackages:
    vite: ^2.5.0-beta.1 => 2.5.0-beta.1
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

### Logs

```shell
> tsc && vite build

error TS18000: Circularity detected while resolving configuration: /home/dominikg/develop/reproductions/vite-ts-vanilla/tsconfig.json -> /home/dominikg/develop/reproductions/vite-ts-vanilla/tsconfig.circle.json -> /home/dominikg/develop/reproductions/vite-ts-vanilla/tsconfig.json
```
